text:
maria: heads-up — we saw a short cluster-wide latency blip in dedicated-pool-us-west around 10:12. p95 token latency jumped ~25% for ~3m, CPU was fine but GPUs showed short stalls. suspects: small bursty egress + nvlink contention.
jon: can you paste the scheduler logs and any `nvidia-smi dmon` output?
maria: pasted below. not a lot in scheduler except a bunch of concurrent tiny batches from several tenants. dmon shows periodic mem reads spikes.
---
```
# nvidia-smi dmon sample
Time        sm    mem%   enc   dec
10:11:58    12     68     0     0
10:12:05    98     72     0     0   <-- spike
10:12:12    10     69     0     0
```
---
jon: hmm those short high SM bursts align with many tiny requests getting scheduled at once. looks like small-batch noisy neighbor.
sasha: is this only on shared slices or are dedicated slots affected too?
maria: dedicated slices impacted when a colocated shared-tenant pod does a synchronous allreduce-ish pattern. it's rare but reproducible in lab if you replay the traffic.
kevin: could be PCIe/host NIC saturation causing backpressure into the GPU. any kernel NIC drops?
maria: some kernel tx_drops around same window on host nic queue 2.
jon: two prongs: 1) fast mitigation: sandbag tenants with short burst backoff — slow-start micro-batching for tenants that open many concurrent small streams; 2) medium: add egress shaping at host NIC for low-QoS tenants.
sasha: +1 for host-level shaping. we already tag QoS on allocs, just need a policing hook in the egress path. keeping it local avoids cross-az routing churn.
kevin: what about prewarming KV cache for ded pockets? many of these stalls are KV miss storms. prewarm might smooth the SM spikes.
maria: prewarm helps but doesn't fix NIC bursts. both needed.
jon: operational question — how do we detect the pattern? propose: a lightweight probe that checks p95 token delta vs expected for tiny batch sizes and emits a "sandbag-suggest" event when correlated with host nic drops.
sasha: we can piggyback on existing telemetry pipeline. create a rule in ingest: if (tenant_concurrent_requests > 50 && mean_batch_size < 8 && host_tx_drops > 10/min) -> flag.
kevin: agree. add a cost tag so billing can reflect protective throttles (avoid surprising customers).
maria: deploy-bot: create incident summary and link to runbook for noisy microburst?
deploy-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2409. Runbook: infra/runbooks/noisy-microburst.md. TTL: 48h. :white_check_mark:
jon: next steps: 1) telemetry rule (sasha) 2) sandbag flow prototype in router (jon+maria) 3) host egress shaping experiment (kevin). aim for canary in canary pool next week.
sasha: i'll own the rule + alert.
maria: i'll start a sandbox branch for sandbag logic, will share a tiny replay script.
kevin: i'll scope the tc/qdisc shaping and a safe defaults patch.
jon: thanks all — copy this thread into eng-sre if we need oncall run tomorrow. :eyes:
